The (Ga,Mn)As nanowires were grown by MBE on the {1100} side facets of wurtzite (Ga,In)As nanowires.
The typical diameter of the (Ga,In)As core is between 70-200 nm.
The thickness of the (Ga,Al)As shell at the bottom part of the NW is about 10 nm.
The thickness of the (Ga,Mn)As/LT-GaAs shells at the bottom part of the NW is 5 nm.
The hole density in the (Ga,Mn)As shells is estimated to be higher than in previous reports.
A non-zero magnetic signal appears below about 25 K.
The spontaneous magnetic moment is the hallmark of the presence of a long-range magnetic order in the investigated material.
A (small) fraction of the mesoscopic volumes got locked into a percolating form.
The average surface density of the NWs is estimated from SEM images to be at the level of 109 cm-2.
The typical length of the NWs is between 3.5-4.0 µm.
The (Ga,Mn)As shells are sandwiched between an inner (Ga,Al)As and outer LT-GaAs shells.
The (Ga,Al)As shell is continuous up to the top of the (Ga,In)As core.
The (Ga,Mn)As shell is continuous even in its thinnest parts.
The Mn distribution in the (Ga,Mn)As shell is homogeneous.
The In content in the (Ga,In)As core is about 10%.
The SF density is in the range 20-60 SF/micrometer of the NW length.
The NWs were grown with Au catalyst on GaAs(111)B substrates.
